settings.storage.snapshotsFolderHint: Where version-history snapshots (ZIP archives) are stored.
settings.storage.safetyFolderHint: A safety copy of your save is taken here before every incoming sync, so a bad sync is always reversible.
settings.storage.autoDeleteHint: The snapshots OpenSave takes on its own — before a sync replaces files, when a game saves, at a conflict. Snapshots you took yourself are kept, and so is the newest one on every branch, whatever its age. Runs shortly after start and every few hours.
settings.storage.maxAuto: Automatic snapshots to keep per game
settings.storage.maxAutoHint: Default limit for newly tracked games (0 = keep everything). The oldest are pruned first, per branch. Change a single game's limit in its Configuration tab.
settings.storage.maxManual: Manual snapshots to keep per game
settings.storage.maxManualHint: Snapshots you take yourself have their own budget, so games that auto-save often (Elden Ring, Dragonsword) can't push them out. {forever}, which is the default.
settings.storage.applyLimits: Apply these limits to every game
settings.storage.applyLimitsHint: Replaces each game's own limits with these, then deletes the snapshots beyond them on every branch. To clean up with each game's own limits, use Space used above.
settings.storage.scanPathsHint: Scanning already checks Steam and common emulators — add custom libraries here.
settings.storage.excludePathsHint: Scans skip these folders and everything inside them — handy for stale save locations (like an old GSE saves directory) you don't want offered again.
settings.reset.title: Reset tracking
settings.reset.hint: Untrack every game at once, then scan again to add them back from the correct locations — useful after moving games between launchers or drives. This only clears the tracking list; your save snapshots on disk are kept.
settings.advanced.daemonPortHint: The port this device listens on, for the app and for your other devices on the network. Changing it requires a restart.
settings.advanced.pathTranslationHint: Rewrites another device's save paths to this one's conventions, e.g. "C:\Users\me\Saves" → "/home/deck/saves".
settings.support.title: Support OpenSave
settings.support.lede: Free and open source, and it stays that way — no accounts, no ads, no telemetry, and nothing locked behind a payment.
settings.support.body: It's built and maintained in spare time. If it's saved you the hassle of copying save folders between machines, you're welcome to chip in.
settings.support.point3: Time for fixes and new features
settings.support.openedToast: Opened in your browser — thank you.
settings.support.foot: Prefer not to donate? Reporting a bug or suggesting a feature helps just as much.
settings.support.note: Payment is handled entirely by Gumroad — OpenSave never sees your card details.
settings.sync.unknownGameHint: Tracking automatically works out a folder from where the game lives on the other device, which is why OpenSave usually needs no setup.

settings.saveState.autosave: Changes save as you make them

settings.reset.confirmBody.other: Untrack all {n} games? They'll be removed from your library so you can re-add them from the correct locations. Your save snapshots on disk are kept — nothing is deleted.

settings.general.typeHint: Shown to other devices when they discover you.
settings.general.libraryHint: How your games are laid out on Home. Changes apply straight away.

settings.general.startOnBootHint: Launches minimized to the system tray so syncing runs in the background.
settings.general.betasOnPreRelease: You're running {version}, which is a beta, so you'll be offered newer betas whether or not this is ticked — otherwise there'd be no way forward until the final release caught up. Untick it and you'll move to the stable release as soon as it's newer than what you have.
settings.general.betasStable: Betas ship early with the newest fixes and are less tested. You'll be offered the stable release whenever it's newer, so this isn't a one-way door.
settings.sync.autoSyncOnTrack: Sync a game immediately when it's first tracked
settings.sync.detectNewGames: Tell me when a game turns up with saves OpenSave isn't keeping
settings.sync.detectNewGamesHint: OpenSave looks every hour, in the background, and only mentions games it hasn't seen before. Nothing is tracked until you choose it.
settings.sync.matchByAppId: Match saves across PCs by Steam App ID
settings.sync.matchByAppIdHint: Links the same game across devices even when it was tracked under different names or drives.
settings.sync.matchByAppIdMore: For example a Steam copy on one PC and a standalone copy on another. Leave this off if you deliberately keep two separate copies of the same game that shouldn't merge. You can always link games by hand from a game's page.
settings.sync.unknownGameLabel: When another device syncs a game this one doesn't have
settings.sync.unknownGame.ask: Ask me where to keep it
settings.sync.unknownGameMore: Choose {askMe} if your saves are somewhere that guess would get wrong — a second drive, a folder you moved, or a game that keeps saves in a folder named after your account. Games waiting for a folder appear on the Home page.
settings.sync.speedHint: Only applies to relay (internet) syncs — LAN is never throttled.
settings.sync.relayUrlHint: The relay that carries syncs across the internet. Join a room from {internetSync}.
settings.sync.hostRelay: Host a WAN relay server on this device
settings.sync.hostRelayHint: Lets friends connect directly to you instead of the public relay.
settings.sync.relayPortHint: Forward this TCP port on your router so friends on the internet can reach you.
settings.sync.cloudBackupHint: Where backups go, whether every snapshot is sent there, and whether newer saves are brought from your other devices are all set on the Cloud Backup page.

protection.detail.direct: This device is reached straight over your local network, so nothing passes through a relay. Local traffic is not encrypted, so treat an untrusted network accordingly.
protection.detail.open: Saves sent to this device over the internet can be read by anyone holding your room code, including whoever runs the relay. Pairing over a relay did not keep an encryption key in older versions. Unpair and pair these two devices again to fix it.
protection.detail.pending: The key is in place. Encryption starts as soon as this device checks in, which usually takes a few seconds.
protection.detail.sealed: Saves sent to this device are sealed between the two of you. The relay — and anyone else holding your room code — passes them on without being able to read them.
protection.fingerprint: Pairing fingerprint {code} — it should read the same on the other device.

pause.pauseTitle: Stop syncing with your other devices for a while — snapshots are still taken
pause.resumeTitle: Syncing is paused {length}. Snapshots are still taken. Resume now to catch up.
conflict.title: Save conflict — {game}
conflict.desc: Both this device and {peer} changed this save since the last sync. Pick which version to play from.
conflict.diffCapped: Counts above cover the first {shown} of {total} differing files.

conflict.broughtHere.one: The {n} file only on {peer} is brought here;
conflict.broughtHere.other: The {n} files only on {peer} are brought here;

conflict.keptWhere: where both have a file, yours is kept.
conflict.deletesTail: that only this device has (snapshotted first).
conflict.deletesNothing: nothing only this device has is lost.
conflict.decideLaterTitle: Nothing of this game syncs until you decide. Open the game to decide.

conflict.keepTheirsTitle.one: Deletes 1 file only this device has
conflict.keepTheirsTitle.other: Deletes {n} files only this device has

conflict.hintAll: Nothing is lost whichever you pick. {both} (recommended) keeps playing yours — {peer} receives it too — and keeps {peer}'s version here on a branch you can switch to. {mine} makes your version the shared one — {peer} receives it (their old save is snapshotted first). {theirs} adopts {peer}'s version here, snapshotting yours first. Restore anything from the game's Snapshots / Branches tabs.
conflict.attentionBody: Its save changed here and on another device at once — choose which to keep.
conflict.attentionToast: Save conflict for “{name}” — choose which version to keep
conflict.applyingToast: Applying your choice for “{name}” — transferring {peer}'s files…
locConflict.title: “{root}” folder — {game}
locConflict.desc: This is one of {game}'s extra save folders, and it changed on both this device and {peer}. The game's main save is unaffected and keeps syncing; only this folder is waiting on you.
locConflict.attentionBody: Its “{root}” folder differs on both devices — choose which to keep.
locConflict.attentionToast: The “{root}” folder of “{game}” differs on both devices
locConflict.decideLaterTitle: Nothing of this folder syncs until you decide. Open the game to decide.
locConflict.hintUndo: A snapshot of every one of this game's folders is taken before either choice is applied, so both are undoable from the Snapshots tab. {mine} makes this device's copy the shared one and asks {peer} to take it — {peer} gets its own say if it has newer work. {theirs} brings their copy here.
locConflict.hintNoKeepBoth: There is no “keep both” for a folder: that option puts the other copy on a branch, and branches cover the whole game rather than one of its folders.

settings.snapshotChecks.removeConfirmBod.other: Remove the {n} snapshots that can't be restored from the history? Their archives are already gone or damaged, so nothing that could be restored is lost; every other snapshot stays.

settings.snapshotChecks.removedToast.one: Removed {n} snapshot that couldn't be restored
settings.snapshotChecks.removedToast.other: Removed {n} snapshots that couldn't be restored

settings.snapshotChecks.damagedBody: Their archives were deleted or damaged outside OpenSave. Every other snapshot is fine, and so is each game's save.
settings.snapshotChecks.okStrong: Every snapshot checked can be restored.
settings.snapshotChecks.lookCloud: Look for copies in the cloud
settings.snapshotChecks.fixHint: With cloud backup on, each snapshot was uploaded as it was taken: a whole copy there is fetched, checked and put back. What has no copy anywhere can only be removed — the record promises a save that no longer exists.
settings.snapshotChecks.firstLater: The first a little after OpenSave starts.
settings.snapshotChecks.scheduleHint: Anything the cloud still has whole is put back as it's found.
settings.snapshotChecks.stillChecked: Snapshots are still checked before they're restored.
settings.snapshotChecks.checkHint: Each is read back in full and every file compared with its checksum. A snapshot is also checked before it is restored.

settings.storageUsage.shareToast.one: {n} snapshot now shares unchanged files · {size} freed
settings.storageUsage.shareToast.other: {n} snapshots now share unchanged files · {size} freed

settings.storageUsage.deleteConfirmBody: Delete the {size} snapshot of {game} from {when}?{pinned} This can't be undone; the current save isn't affected.
settings.storageUsage.pinnedNote: It is pinned, so nothing else would ever have removed it.

settings.storageUsage.reclaimHint.one: {n} snapshot is past a game's limits, on an old conflict branch, or past the age rule. Pinned snapshots are never among them.
settings.storageUsage.reclaimHint.other: {n} snapshots are past a game's limits, on an old conflict branch, or past the age rule. Pinned snapshots are never among them.

settings.storageUsage.savingLess: {size} less, because older snapshots keep the files they have in common once rather than each keeping its own copy.
settings.storageUsage.sharingExplain: Older snapshots keep the files they have in common once rather than each keeping its own copy, so a game with many save slots doesn't store every slot again in every snapshot.
settings.storageUsage.newestComplete: The newest snapshot of each branch and pinned ones keep complete copies of their own.
devices.title: Devices
devices.nonePairedHint: Pair a device below — on your Wi-Fi it appears automatically, or connect over the internet with a room code.
devices.unpairConfirmBody: Unpair "{name}"? Their games stay on both devices; syncing between you stops.
devices.repairConfirmBody: Unpair "{name}", then pair the two devices again so they exchange an encryption key. Their games and saves stay where they are. Nothing syncs between these two devices until you pair them again.
devices.repairConfirmTitle: Unpair, so you can pair again?
devices.repairToast: Unpaired {name} — pair the two devices again to encrypt what you sync
devices.updateConfirmBody: {name} is running a newer OpenSave build ({version}). Download it from {name} and update this device? OpenSave restarts itself when done.

devices.lanEmpty: No unpaired devices found on the local network. Make sure OpenSave is running on the other device.
app.emptiedToast: Every save file of {name} was deleted here. Your other devices keep theirs until you choose.
app.emptiedBody: Every save file was deleted here. Your other devices keep theirs until you choose.
app.restartNote: The app restarts itself when done — your games keep syncing.

game.header.openFolderTitle: Show this folder in your file manager

game.header.deleteEverywhereMsg.one: Delete {name}'s save files on your other devices too? {n} file there will go; each device keeps a snapshot of them first.
game.header.deleteEverywhereMsg.other: Delete {name}'s save files on your other devices too? {n} files there will go; each device keeps a snapshot of them first.

game.header.puttingBackDevices: Putting {name}'s files back — {n} come from your other devices
game.header.emptiedFetchingBody: Some are still to come from your other devices; this game syncs as usual once they're all here.
game.header.emptiedTitle: Every save file in {where} was deleted on this device.
game.header.emptiedBody: Your other devices still have theirs, and nothing is synced until you choose.
game.header.putBackFromSnapshot: Put them back from the snapshot of {when}, with anything newer from your other devices
game.header.putBackFromDevices: Put them back from your other devices
game.header.orDeleteThere: — or, if you meant it, delete them there too; each device keeps a snapshot first.
game.header.deleteThereBtn: Delete them on my other devices too
game.header.elsewhereTitle: This game isn't on this device.
game.header.elsewhereBody: Its saves are on {drive}, which this PC doesn't have, so it's skipped here and keeps syncing between your other devices. If it is installed here, point the game at its save folder with Edit.
game.header.folderMissingTitle: This save folder is not there.
game.header.folderMissingBody: It may have been moved or deleted, or be on a drive that isn't connected. Nothing is snapshotted or synced for this game until it's back — OpenSave picks it up again within a minute. If the save lives somewhere else now, point the game at it with Edit.
game.header.relocateBody: Is that where this game saves on this device? Only use it if it holds your current saves, not an old copy.
game.appId.label: Steam App ID
game.appId.hint: The number in the game's Steam store URL. Used to launch it and fetch its cover art.
game.appId.moreInfo1: With “Match games by Steam App ID” turned on in Settings, it also lets this game sync with a copy tracked under a different name on another device. Filled in automatically when it can be worked out; a save under
game.appId.moreInfo2: often has nothing to work it out from, so you can set it here.
game.appId.unknown1: No Steam game has this App ID. It's the number in the store page address —
game.appId.unknown2: — not the one from another store.
game.appId.unreachable: Couldn't reach Steam to check this number. If Steam's store or CDN is blocked on this network, cover art won't load here either — the ID itself may well be right.
game.locations.title: Save locations
game.locations.hint: Some games keep their save split across more than one folder — the save data in one place, settings or mods in another. Add each extra folder here and it is synced, snapshotted and restored along with the main one.
game.locations.noFolder: no folder on this device — this location isn't being synced
game.locations.name: name
game.locations.matchHint2: on your other devices — that is what the two sides match on, since the folder lives somewhere different on each machine. Removing a location here never deletes its files.
game.locations.removedUndo: The “{name}” folder is no longer covered. Its files are left where they are.
game.manage.linkedDesc: If this game is tracked under a different name or drive on another PC (e.g. a Steam copy vs. a portable copy), link the copies so their saves sync across devices. Linking merges another tracked game here into this one: its save files stay where they are, and its snapshots move here, onto a branch named after it.
game.manage.chooseToLink: Choose a game above to link
game.manage.nothingToLink: Nothing to link to. Track the other copy on this device, or pair the device that has it and make sure it's online — its games appear here once it answers.
game.manage.linkRemoteMsg: Link "{name}" on {peer} to "{game}"? The two will be treated as the same game when these devices sync. Nothing on either device is removed.
game.manage.linkLocalMsg: Link "{name}" into "{game}"? They'll be treated as the same game when syncing across devices. "{name}" leaves your library here — its save files stay where they are, and its snapshots move to "{game}", on a branch of their own.
game.manage.stopTrackingDesc: Removes "{name}" from OpenSave. Your save files and existing snapshot archives on disk are kept.
game.branches.hint: A branch is a separate line of saves — a second playthrough, or a run you want to keep apart from your main one. You'll be asked what it starts from.
game.branches.createdFromCurrent: Branch created from your current save
game.branches.deleteConfirm: Delete branch "{name}" and all its snapshots? Your current save and other branches aren't affected.
game.branches.footnote: Switching branches snapshots your current save first, then restores the other branch's latest state. A branch you just created has no state of its own yet, so it starts from whatever is in your save folder now — the two diverge from the first snapshot you take on it.
game.newBranch.title: New branch — {name}
game.newBranch.question: What should it start from?
game.newBranch.copyTitle: A copy of my current save
game.newBranch.copyDesc: "{name}" begins exactly where you are now. The two only diverge from the first snapshot you take on it — so this is the one for trying something without losing your place.
game.newBranch.freshDesc1: "{name}" begins empty, for a new playthrough from scratch. Switching to it clears your save folder — your current save is snapshotted first and comes straight back when you switch to
game.newBranch.hint: Either way nothing is lost. Switching between branches snapshots whatever is in your save folder first, and refuses to change anything if that snapshot can't be taken.
game.compare.title: Compare snapshots

game.compare.noDiff.one: No difference: the same {n} file in both.
game.compare.noDiff.other: No difference: the same {n} files in both.

game.link.onThisDeviceNote: Its entry here merges into this one
game.link.onOtherDevicesNote: Nothing is removed on either device
game.config.title: Launch & sync configuration
game.config.saveFolderHint: The folder OpenSave treats as this game's save.
game.config.saveFolderMore2: this folder, so each device can point at a different path and still end up with the same files — useful when a game keeps saves in a per-account folder named after your Steam or Epic ID, which differs on every machine. Point each device at its own such folder and saves land where that copy of the game looks for them.
game.config.saveFolderNotSaved: Not saved yet. The old folder keeps its files but stops syncing and being snapshotted.
game.config.appIdError: A Steam App ID is digits only — the number in the store URL.
game.config.exePathHint: Launch starts this, even for a Steam game. Leave it empty to launch through Steam.
game.config.coverUrlHint: Leave blank to auto-use Steam art from the App ID. Paste any image URL for emulators.
game.config.autoSync: Auto-sync saves when changes are detected
game.config.maxHint2: snapshots kept per branch (0 = unlimited). Oldest are pruned first.
game.config.manualHint1: Snapshots you took yourself get their own budget, so a game that auto-saves often can't push them out.
game.config.moveTrackTitle: Move tracking to a new folder?
game.config.moveTrackConfirm:
Track “{name}” at {path} from now on?

Files in the old folder are left exactly where they are, but they stop syncing and stop being snapshotted. Existing snapshots are kept and still restore.
game.ignore.title: Files that shouldn't sync
game.ignore.desc: Some games keep device-specific settings in the same folder as the save, and copying those to another machine can break the game there. List them here and they stay put: never sent, never received, never deleted by a sync.
game.ignore.patterns1: One pattern per line, like a
game.ignore.patterns7: for an exception. Case doesn't matter. Set the same list on your other devices; each one applies its own.
game.ignore.stillBackedUp2: , so a restore brings them back — excluding something stops it travelling, it never stops it being backed up.
game.ignore.empty: This game's folders are empty, so there is nothing to pick yet.
game.ignore.tickHint1: Ticking a file writes the pattern for you, anchored so it can only ever mean that one file. Unticking a file caught by a wildcard adds a

internetSync.lead: Sync across the internet with no port forwarding: both devices join the same room code on a relay, and the connection to it is encrypted. The relay stores nothing — no copy of a save is written to it.
internetSync.sealedBefore: Saves are sealed between your two devices, so the relay passes on data it cannot read — not even ours. It can still see that two devices are talking, roughly how much data moves, and which games by id. Running
internetSync.repairNote: Both devices need a recent version for this, and internet pairings made before it need to be made again: pairing over a relay never kept the key, so an older pair still sends in the clear. Unpair and pair those two devices again to protect them. Pairings made over a local network kept their key and are unaffected.
internetSync.statusIdleHintBefore: Enter a room code below and press
internetSync.statusIdleHintAfter: to start syncing over the internet.
internetSync.waitingForOther: Waiting for your other device to join with the same code.
internetSync.encNone: Devices you pair here sync encrypted end to end, so nobody else holding this code — including the relay — can read your saves. Both devices need this version; each one shows its own state here and under Devices once it's paired.
internetSync.encAll: Saves to {target} here are encrypted — nobody else in this room can read them.
internetSync.encWarnBefore: Saves sent through this room are
internetSync.encWarnAfter: , so anyone holding this room code can read them. Pair {target} again to fix it.
internetSync.encMixed: {done} of {total} paired devices here are encrypted. Pair the {target} again to protect {pron} too.
internetSync.connectingHint: Free-hosted relays can take up to a minute to wake from sleep — hang tight, we retry automatically.

internetSync.relayLockedAfter: environment variable, so it can't be changed here. Change the variable and restart OpenSave, or unset it to go back to the saved setting.

internetSync.noDevicesYet: No other devices in the room yet. Enter the same code on your other device and it will appear here.
